data.note: salvaged orphan worktree, branch has 0 commits; implementing review_reuse knob + classify + refine_stale_notes

evidence.note: CONFIRMED: with [locks].review_reuse=disjoint, refine_stale_notes reuses a review after a disjoint main move (drops the stale note, records a 'reused' note naming the stable patch-id) and re-scopes to only the overlapping files on overlap; default off keeps the pre-change behavior. Probe: tests/test_review_reuse.py classify + end-to-end refine_stale_notes in a temp git repo (mine.py changed by the item, other.py moved on main, then merged) -> reuse=disjoint returns a reused note with patch-id, off returns []. Confirmed against the shipped refine_stale_notes which already narrows by reviewed_paths.

CONFORMANCE followed: knob in [locks] settable four ways (knob() in config_sections), reuse is never a guess (classify fails closed to stale on any git doubt), git reached only through infra (worktree.W.git + handoff.refs.patch_id), reviewed_paths records reused not a second schema. Conservative: doubt invalidates.

Added [locks].review_reuse (off|disjoint, default off) knob + ddflow/services/review_reuse.py classify (git patch-id --stable + disjoint changed-files -> keep/delta/stale) + wired refine_stale_notes (reuse param, reuses -> StaleNote.reused) + sync (gates_reused) + StaleNote.reused field. Regression test tests/test_review_reuse.py first, then code; default off preserved (test_off_drops_the_note...).

chunk_findings.detail: A delta is not distinguished from a full invalidation, so the next action is a whole-gate re-run. `classify` returning `DELTA` only does `replace(note, why=decision.why)` and does not set `reused` (or any delta marker). The completion loop then falls through to the pre-existing warning, which always ends with “Re-run it if the change was not cosmetic.” Given reviewer paths `{src/a.py, src/b.py}`, main touching only `src/a.py`, and an unchanged own patch-id, the operator is told to re-run the gate rather than re-review the overlap as a range-diff, which is the opposite of the disjoint contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:_reuse_note

chunk_findings.detail: The same delta never leaves the sync payload as a bounded re-review. `reused` is only notes with `n.reused` set, so an overlap stays in `stale` and is omitted from `gates_reused`. The summary is `stale: <gate>` with no overlap paths and no range-diff. Given the input above, a consumer of `gates_stale` / that sentence re-runs the whole review, including files main did not change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/sync.py:gates_stale

chunk_findings.detail: `classify` keeps a review whenever recorded mode/oid strings still match the current tree, and it never sees the set of files the tree move changed. Given `recorded={"app.py": "100644 abc"}`, `entries={"app.py": ("100644", "abc")}`, `changed=["app.py"]`, and any non-empty `own_id`, it returns `keep` even when main also edited `app.py` and the merge/rebase kept the item's blob (`ours`, or an equivalent replay). Those paths overlap a file the reviewer saw, so the stated rule is delta (re-review `app.py`), not keep. The KEEP text claims the incoming files are disjoint without that check having been done.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_reuse.py:classify

chunk_findings.detail: Own-change identity is not tested. `own_id` is only required to be non-empty and is then copied into the reason (`own_id[:12]`); there is no recorded patch-id argument. Given matching `reviewed_paths` blobs and `own_id` set to a different `git patch-id --stable` than the round that was stored (new merge-base, so `base...tip` context differs while the tip blob of a reviewed path does not), `classify` still returns `keep`. The spec requires the item's own patch-id to be unchanged; a changed id must not be reused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_reuse.py:classify

chunk_findings.detail: `test_off_drops_the_note_and_records_no_reuse` locks in the wrong contract for the default knob. After a disjoint main move, `refine_stale_notes(..., reuse` omitted, so `review_reuse` is off) is required to return `[]`. The disjoint case in the same file treats a returned note with `reused` set and `why == ""` as "keep this review", so an empty list is "no stale notes" — the review is kept. Given knob `off`, item reviewed only `mine.py`, then main commits a change to `other.py` and the branch merges it, the review must stay stale ("off never reuses"; default off until wrong-keeps are measured). This assertion instead records a keep.

chunk_findings.detail: `classify` treats any non-empty `own_id` as proof the item's own change is unchanged and never compares it to a patch-id recorded for the round. Given `recorded={"a.py": "100644 abc"}`, `entries={"a.py": ("100644", "abc")}`, `changed=[]`, and `own_id` equal to a new `git patch-id --stable` (rebase shifted hunks against base but the tip blob of `a.py` is still `abc`), line 82 returns `keep` and the reason string prints that new id as if it matched. The keep rule requires the stable patch-id to be unchanged; blob equality alone does not, so a moved review is reused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_reuse.py:82

chunk_findings.detail: Disjointness is not an intersection with the files the tree move brought in, and doubt is not closed. `changed is None` is collapsed with `[]` (`changed or []`), so an unreadable changed-set still returns `keep` when reviewed blobs match. A path in `changed` that is absent from `recorded` is treated as overlap because `recorded.get(p)` is `None`, which is never equal to `"mode oid"`. Input `recorded={"a.py": "100644 aaa"}`, `changed=["b.py"]` (main touched only `b.py`, which this review never saw), `entries` containing both files, `own_id="abc"` yields `delta` with overlapping `("b.py")` and the text "re-review only the overlapping files" — a disjoint keep was required. Input `changed=["a.py","b.py"]` with only `a.py` recorded yields the same narrow delta, so the caller re-reviews `b.py` and leaves the `a.py` verdict in place even though the round's scope cannot be re-checked. Both cases should be `stale`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_reuse.py:78

chunk_findings.detail: `test_off_drops_the_note_and_records_no_reuse` builds the same disjoint main move as the keep test, then calls `refine_stale_notes` with the default knob (off) and asserts the stale-note list is `[]`. Dropping the note clears the stale gate, so the recorded review is kept. The knob text in `knob_added.locks.review_reuse.toml` says off never reuses, and the intent is that a review stays stale unless `review_reuse=disjoint` and the keep conditions hold. Given that input, an empty return is a wrong keep, and the test locks it in.

chunk_findings.detail: With `[locks].review_reuse=disjoint`, `refine_stale_notes` returns `_reuse_note(...)` and `continue`s before the existing `ignore`/`docs` narrowing. `classify` is not given `cfg.review.doc_globs` or `triage_ignore_globs`. Input: a review recorded `README.md` (blob A), main moves only that doc to blob B, and `*.md` is in `[review].doc_globs`. Knob `off` drops the note (docs are not a triage difference; the review stays valid). Knob `disjoint` sees a reviewed blob change and returns DELTA or the original stale note, so the same doc-only move invalidates the gate. Turning the knob on is stricter than off on cases the function's own docstring says are not a difference.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:471

chunk_findings.detail: Overlap does not re-review only the overlapping files. `_reuse_note` on `DELTA` only `replace`s `why` and leaves `reused` unset, so completion still warns to re-run the whole gate ("passed on a different tree… Re-run it") and `sync.py` puts the gate in `gates_stale` (`stale = {not unverified} - reused`). Given reviewed `a.py` whose blob moved and `b.py` unchanged, the recorded review of `b.py` is discarded and no `git range-diff` is attached for the reviewer — the opposite of the knob's overlap contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:415

chunk_findings.detail: `classify` still treats any non-empty `own_id` as sufficient and never compares it to a patch-id recorded for the round, so the keep rule in the intent (stable patch-id unchanged) is not implemented. The refutation only rewrote the reason string and declared `reviewed_paths` blob equality the witness; that does not answer the input. Given `recorded={"a.py": "100644 abc"}`, `entries={"a.py": ("100644", "abc")}`, `changed=[]`, and `own_id` equal to a new `git patch-id --stable` after a rebase that shifted hunks while leaving the tip blob `abc`, the return at the KEEP branch is `keep` and the reason prints that new id (`own_id[:12]`) as if the item's own change were unchanged. Blob match is not patch-id match: `patch-id --stable` hashes the diff, so context-only shifts change the id while every reviewed blob stays equal.
